previous_attempt_summaries.strategy_summary: Reduce the global lower bound on the number of descents of the modular-inverse permutation to a local obstruction: prove that five consecutive inverse values can never be strictly increasing. This implies that every block of four consecutive indices contains a descent. A purely combinatorial covering lemma then yields at least ceil((p-2)/4) descents, and for odd primes this equals floor(p/4), which is stronger than the required bound > p/4 - 1.
previous_attempt_summaries.vet_summary: The plan is not acceptable as stated because two lemmas are false: L5 fails for small N (in particular N = 3, which is exactly the p = 5 boundary case), and L6 is false for primes p congruent to 3 mod 4.
